cohort: The study included parturient women identified with pulmonary aspiration (cases) from UK consultant-led obstetric units and control women from other UKOSS studies.
finding: Pulmonary aspiration is rare in UK obstetric anaesthetic practice, with an incidence of 5.2 per 1,000,000 maternities, but remains a risk of general anaesthesia.
mod_finding: Women who experienced pulmonary aspiration were significantly more likely to undergo caesarean section and to receive general anaesthesia for caesarean section.
